title: MigQL snippet
description: A migration snippet of MIG-Ace: a file that ends in .migql.yaml.

migration.description: The name of the snippet: `YYYYMMDD-HHMM-slug`. Snippets run in the order of their names.

repair.description: The name of a repair snippet. It corrects what an earlier snippet did, where a condition says so.

uid.description: The identity of the snippet. It is created once and never changes; the database remembers the snippet by it.

doc.description: One sentence that says what the snippet is for.

when.description: Runs the snippet or the part only if the condition is true. Otherwise it is skipped and looked at again on the next run.

let.description: Names for conditions that are used more than once.

parts.description: The steps of the snippet, in the order in which they run. Every part has a name and one operation.

testdata.description: Rows that the proof inserts after the snippet ran, so that later snippets work on filled tables.

testdata-before.description: Rows that the proof inserts before the snippet runs, in the old shape of the tables.

changed.description: The reason for an intended change to a released snippet. Without it the build rejects the change.

retired.description: The snippet never runs again. Databases that ran it keep their record.

requires-downtime.description: The snippet may only run while the application is stopped.

do.description: One statement in the statement language. It is checked and then translated for the database.

column-ensure.description:
Makes sure that a column exists with at least the given type.

## Result

The column exists and has exactly the given type after the action, whether it was missing, narrower or already right.

## Parameters

| Parameter | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `table` | The table that gets the column. |
| `column` | The name of the column. |
| `type` | The type the column must have, for example `varchar(500)`. |
| `default` | Optional. The default value of the column, used when the column is added. |
| `not-null` | Optional. `true` makes the column mandatory when it is added. |

## PostgreSQL

One block of code that decides in the database:

- The column is missing: it is added.
- The column has the type: nothing happens.
- The column is narrower: it is widened. This holds for a longer `varchar` or `char`, and for a `numeric` with a larger precision and the same scale.
- Anything else: the part fails with a message that shows the type the column has.

## Locks

Adding a column without a default and widening a `varchar` change only the catalog; the strong lock on the table is held for a moment. Widening a `numeric` can rewrite the table and holds the lock meanwhile.

## After a failure

The action is one step and one transaction. After a failure nothing is changed, and the next run decides again.

## Notes

- No condition is needed around this action. It says what is wanted.
- `default` and `not-null` are used only when the column is added. An existing column keeps its own.

table.description: The table that gets the column.

type.description: The type the column must have, for example `varchar(500)`.

default.description: Optional. The default value of the column, used when the column is added.

not-null.description: Optional. `true` makes the column mandatory when it is added.

column-rename.description:
Gives a column another name.

## Result

The column has the new name. Its values, its type and its constraints stay.

## Parameters

| Parameter | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `table` | The table of the column. |
| `from` | The name the column has now. |
| `to` | The new name. |

## PostgreSQL

In a run without a phase: one statement, `alter table … rename column … to …`.

With the phases `start` and `finish`, a second column and a trigger keep older application versions working. That form comes with the upgrade phases.

## Locks

The rename changes only the catalog. The strong lock on the table is held for a moment.

## After a failure

The action is one step. After a failure nothing is changed, and the next run tries again.

## Notes

- A change of case only, such as `key` to `Key`, is an ordinary rename.
- An older application version that uses the old name stops working after a plain rename.

from.description: The name the column has now.

column-set-not-null.description:
Makes a column mandatory without blocking the table while its rows are read.

## Result

The column is `not null`. Every row must have a value before; fill the rows in an earlier part.

## Parameters

| Parameter | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `table` | The table of the column. |
| `column` | The column that becomes mandatory. |

## PostgreSQL

Four steps:

1. A check constraint `<table>_<column>_not_null` that says the column is not null, added as not valid.
2. The validation of that constraint.
3. `alter table … alter column … set not null`. PostgreSQL sees the valid constraint and does not read the table again.
4. The removal of the constraint.

## Locks

Steps 1, 3 and 4 take the strong lock on the table for a moment. Step 2 reads all rows under a lock that lets everybody read and write.

## After a failure

- Step 1 fails if a constraint with the helper name exists already. Nothing is changed then.
- Step 2 fails if a row has no value. The helper constraint stays, not valid. Fill the rows and run again; the run continues with step 2.
- After a failure in step 3 or 4 the next run continues there.

## Notes

- The plain statement `alter table … alter column … set not null` under `do` is one step. It reads the whole table under the strong lock.

constraint-add-check.description:
Adds a check constraint without blocking the table while its rows are checked.

## Result

The check constraint exists and is valid. Every row must fulfil the condition.

## Parameters

| Parameter | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `name` | The name of the constraint. The second step needs it. |
| `table` | The table that gets the constraint. |
| `check` | The condition that every row must fulfil, for example `price_cents >= 0`. An expression is written in the block form. |

## PostgreSQL

Two steps:

1. The constraint is added as not valid. New and changed rows are checked from now on.
2. The validation of the constraint checks the rows that exist.

## Locks

Step 1 takes the strong lock on the table for a moment. Step 2 reads the rows under a lock that lets everybody read and write.

## After a failure

- Step 2 fails if a row does not fulfil the condition. The constraint stays, not valid. Correct the rows and run again; the run continues with step 2.

## Notes

- The plain statement `alter table … add constraint … check (…)` under `do` is one step. It checks all rows under the strong lock.
- State what you assume with `verify-before`, so that the message names the rows that are wrong.

name.description: The name of the constraint. The second step needs it.

table.description: The table that gets the constraint.

check.description: The condition that every row must fulfil, for example `price_cents >= 0`. An expression is written in the block form.

constraint-add-foreign-key.description:
Adds a foreign key without blocking the table while its rows are checked.

## Result

The foreign key exists and is valid. Every row must point to an existing row of the other table.

## Parameters

| Parameter | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `name` | The name of the constraint. The second step needs it. |
| `table` | The table that gets the foreign key. |
| `columns` | The column that points to the other table, or a list of columns: `[book_id, currency]`. |
| `references` | The table that is pointed to. |
| `referenced-columns` | Optional. The columns of the other table. Without it, its primary key. |

## PostgreSQL

Two steps:

1. The constraint is added as not valid. New and changed rows are checked from now on.
2. The validation of the constraint checks the rows that exist.

## Locks

Step 1 takes a strong lock on both tables for a moment. Step 2 reads the rows under a lock that lets everybody read and write.

## After a failure

- Step 2 fails if a row points to nothing. The constraint stays, not valid. Correct the rows and run again; the run continues with step 2.

## Notes

- The plain statement `alter table … add constraint … foreign key …` under `do` is one step. It checks all rows under its lock.
- A rule for a deleted row, such as `on delete cascade`, has no parameter yet. Use the plain statement in a `native` part until it has.

name.description: The name of the constraint. The second step needs it.

table.description: The table that gets the foreign key.

columns.description: The column that points to the other table, or a list of columns: `[book_id, currency]`.

references.description: The table that is pointed to.

referenced-columns.description: Optional. The columns of the other table. Without it, its primary key.

insert.description: Inserts rows, written as YAML: `into`, and `values` for one row or `rows` for several.

upsert.description: Inserts the rows that are missing and updates the rows that exist, found by `key`. Written with `into`, `key` and `rows`.

key.description: The column by which an existing row is found, or a list of columns: `[book_id, currency]`.

native.description: SQL in the dialect of one database, one entry per database. It is sent as it is.

stop.description: Ends the run with a message for a person, for a case that cannot be repaired automatically.

when.description: Runs the snippet or the part only if the condition is true. Otherwise it is skipped and looked at again on the next run.

verify-before.description: Fails the part before it runs if the condition is not true. Nothing is changed then.

verify-after.description: Fails the part after it ran if the condition is not true. Its change is undone.

batch.description: Runs a data statement in portions and saves after each: `20000 by id`. An interrupted run continues with the next portion.

expect-rows.description: How many rows the statement may change: `0..50`. Outside this range the part fails and nothing is changed.

phase.description: `finish` marks a part that breaks older application versions. It runs only when no older version is left.

todo.description: An open decision. The migration script cannot be built while a todo is left.
